candidate.rationale:
Decision on the registered edit: ABANDON (not modify, not retain-as-written). The intended edit was to delete the additive quadratic term and simplify to 2 parameters. The frozen probe resolved it: delta_nmse = 5.48e-04 > epsilon = 1e-05, verdict 'supported', with sham_delta_nmse = 0.0 (so no drift artifact) and all three arms converging (original/canonical_full nmse = 0.09639217003, removed nmse = 0.09694020965). That is ~55x the epsilon threshold and 4 orders of magnitude above the 1e-10 tolerance, so the result sits well inside the supported band rather than the 'unknown' near-threshold band. The registered predicted_delta_nmse of 0.005 was the right sign but overstated the magnitude by roughly an order of magnitude.

Objective consequences. The simplify branch requires n_params < 3 with NMSE increase < 1e-05; the measured increase is 5.48e-04, about 55x too large. So this simplification is dead. The improve branch requires NMSE gain > 1e-10 at n_params = 3, which the current form already attains.

Why I submit the unchanged 3-parameter form rather than an expansion: I have one negative, well-supported probe result and zero positive evidence for any additional term. My reasoning at registration about the x-binned RMSE variation (0.0169, 0.0229, 0.0181, 0.0234) and the nonzero standardized bias (0.0121) pointed only to 'possibly curvature or systematic offset', which is equally consistent with bin-level noise at 2500 rows per bin and heteroscedastic noise. Adding a cubic or v^2 term on that basis would be a guess, not a measurement; it would spend my single submission on an unverified hypothesis. Since the current expression is also confirmed to be the canonical_full arm that refits reproducibly from all-one init with no convergence trouble, it is the best-supported configuration available.

Uncertainty and scope. I have not evaluated this submission; I make no claim that it succeeds. My prediction below is just the already-measured canonical_full train NMSE under an identical refit, expected to reproduce but not guaranteed. This is a development observation on the fixed training split only: it is not a held-out accuracy claim, not a statement that the true generating equation is linear-plus-quadratic, and not evidence that the quadratic term is physically necessary. The probe says this term is useful for train fit under this fitting procedure; that is a weaker statement than necessity.

candidate.rationale:
Decision on the registered edit: ABANDON (not modify, not retain-as-written). The intended edit was to delete the additive quadratic term and simplify to 2 parameters. The frozen probe resolved it: delta_nmse = 5.48e-04 > epsilon = 1e-05, verdict 'supported', with sham_delta_nmse = 0.0 (so no drift artifact) and all three arms converging (original/canonical_full nmse = 0.09639217003, removed nmse = 0.09694020965). That is ~55x the epsilon threshold and 4 orders of magnitude above the 1e-10 tolerance, so the result sits well inside the supported band rather than the 'unknown' near-threshold band. The registered predicted_delta_nmse of 0.005 was the right sign but overstated the magnitude by roughly an order of magnitude.

Objective consequences. The simplify branch requires n_params < 3 with NMSE increase < 1e-05; the measured increase is 5.48e-04, about 55x too large. So this simplification is dead. The improve branch requires NMSE gain > 1e-10 at n_params = 3, which the current form already attains.

Why I submit the unchanged 3-parameter form rather than an expansion: I have one negative, well-supported probe result and zero positive evidence for any additional term. My reasoning at registration about the x-binned RMSE variation (0.0169, 0.0229, 0.0181, 0.0234) and the nonzero standardized bias (0.0121) pointed only to 'possibly curvature or systematic offset', which is equally consistent with bin-level noise at 2500 rows per bin and heteroscedastic noise. Adding a cubic or v^2 term on that basis would be a guess, not a measurement; it would spend my single submission on an unverified hypothesis. Since the current expression is also confirmed to be the canonical_full arm that refits reproducibly from all-one init with no convergence trouble, it is the best-supported configuration available.

Uncertainty and scope. I have not evaluated this submission; I make no claim that it succeeds. My prediction below is just the already-measured canonical_full train NMSE under an identical refit, expected to reproduce but not guaranteed. This is a development observation on the fixed training split only: it is not a held-out accuracy claim, not a statement that the true generating equation is linear-plus-quadratic, and not evidence that the quadratic term is physically necessary. The probe says this term is useful for train fit under this fitting procedure; that is a weaker statement than necessity.

auxiliary.probe_verdict_interpretation: delta_nmse 5.48e-04 > epsilon 1e-05 by ~55x, sham delta 0.0, all arms converged => registered simplify edit is refuted as an improvement route; abandon it.
auxiliary.rationale_confidence: High that the registered simplification fails its objective bar; the probe was decisive and drift-free.
auxiliary.residual_evidence_assessment: Non-monotone x-binned RMSE and nonzero standardized bias are consistent with either real curvature or bin-level noise / heteroscedasticity at n=2500 per bin; not sufficient to justify adding a term without a fit.
